title: Commit + Burst Time-Smoothing Pricing Pilot for Dedicated GPU Capacity
creator: Asha Patel
description: Run a two-arm pilot that evaluates a blended pricing product for Dedicated GPU capacity: long-term commit baseline + time-of-day burst credits with smoothing windows. The goal is to reduce sticker shock for enterprise buyers while preserving predictable revenue and offering measurable SLO tiers (Bronze/Silver/Gold). This ticket captures the PM plan, success metrics, contract/legal asks, telemetry requirements, and rollout steps for a 90-day pilot with 3 reference customers.
acceptance_criteria: Define a clear pricing matrix: commit tier (vGPU-equivalent) x burst credit pool x time-of-day smoothing discount for non-peak hours
Signed pilot addendum template from Legal that covers burst accounting, overage treatment, and SLA ladder with credits
Engineering delivers billing hooks and telemetry: utilization heatmap, per-hour capacity draw, burst credit burn rate, and SLA-attainment dashboards
Two enterprise customers onboarded to pilot, with baseline telemetry for 14 days before activation
Run 30-day experiment and produce ROI report: change in effective utilization, customer cost savings, Redwood revenue delta, and impact on latency/SLOs
tasks: PM: finalize pricing matrix and customer-facing pitch deck
Eng: implement burst-credit accounting and time-of-day smoothing window in billing service (ENG-37412)
Eng: expose telemetry endpoints and dashboard queries for pilot customers
Legal: draft pilot addendum and security questionnaire responses (LEGAL-1182)
Solutions: prepare onboarding runbook and alerting thresholds
Finance: simulate revenue scenarios for 3-year term equivalents
comments: 2025-02-14 Asha Patel: Initial RFC posted. Hypothesis: blending on-peak commit with discounted off-peak burst reduces effective price per token for customers with diurnal workloads and increases committed revenue. Seeking eng and legal feasibility.

2025-02-18 Diego Marquez (Engineering): Feasibility OK. Need 2 weeks to add burst-credit ledger and hooks into invoicing pipeline. KV-cache and autoscale interactions noted — might need fallback model routing when burst exhausted.

2025-02-20 Priya Nair (Legal): Drafting pilot addendum. Key asks: explicit overage calculation, data residency assurances for Dedicated, and audit-rights language. Will include standard security questionnaire attachments.
2025-02-22 Evan Chen: Narrowed pilot to two reference customers (RetailAI Inc., DocAssist Corp.) for initial run. Both expressed interest in time-of-day discounts.

2025-02-24 Product review: Decided to run a two-arm test (A: fixed commit + on-demand; B: commit + burst credits with smoothing). A/B will be measured for cost-per-inference, 95th-latency, and perceived value in customer interviews.
2025-02-26 Solutions-engineer note: Onboarding checklist drafted in Drive. Need customer traffic traces and expected diurnal profile before activation.
2025-02-28 Finance comment: Built a revenue simulation spreadsheet (link below) showing worst-case 6% ARR dilution if burst is heavily utilized; acceptable within guardrails for pilot.

Postmortem/next-steps placeholder: If pilot meets thresholds (>=8% lift in committed revenue or >=12% reduction in average customer token price with SLO attainment >= 99%), propose productization and two new SLA tiers.
